sections.h2: What does the Lake County Recorder do?
sections.html:
The Lake County Recorder records and preserves public land records, including deeds, mortgages, liens, releases, leases and subdivision plats. The office also takes articles of incorporation, assumed business names, military discharges and UCC filings.

It generally does not handle court orders, decrees, judgments, wills, marriage licenses or birth and death certificates. If you are selling a house that came through an estate, the court file and the recorded deed are kept in different places, so expect to visit both.

Records can be viewed or purchased at lcrecorder.com, and staff speak Spanish and use sign language, according to the county's page.

sections.h2: Where is the Lake County Recorder's office and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Recorder is on the second floor of Building A at 2293 N. Main Street in Crown Point, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

sections.h2: What does Indiana law say about recording fees?
sections.html:
Indiana Code 36-2-7-10 sets the recorder's fee schedule. In the 2025 Justia copy, recording a deed or other instrument other than a mortgage costs $25, and a mortgage costs $55.

ServiceFee under IC 36-2-7-10
Deed or other instrument (not a mortgage)$25
Mortgage$55
Page larger than 8.5 by 14 inches$25 for the first page, $5 for each additional
Each added transaction on a release, partial release or assignment$7 on top of the $25 fee
Copy up to 11 by 17 inches$1 per page
Copy larger than 11 by 17 inches$5 per page
Acknowledging or certifying a document$5

Counties may add some charges by ordinance, such as an affordable housing fee of up to $10 per document. That Justia copy may not be current, and the statute requires the recorder to post the fee schedule, so confirm the total with the office or your title company before closing.

One more fee matters on tax-related releases. For a release of a political subdivision's lien on property sold or transferred under the tax sale and redevelopment statutes, the statute lists $25 per parcel for each subdivision with a lien.

sections.h2: What fees does Lake County add for online access and e-recording?
sections.html:
A Lake County ordinance sets a few charges tied to the Recorder. Searching the Recorder's website costs $3 per request, with $1 going to the vendor and $2 to the Recorder's Enhanced Access Fund. Printed pages from requested documents cost $1 each, and the ordinance also lists $3 for e-recording. Credit card charges vary by card company.

Because ordinances are amended often, ask the Recorder to confirm current amounts.

sections.h2: How does e-recording work in Lake County?
sections.html:
Lake County has accepted electronic recordings since March 2021, and the county says it receives over half of its documents that way. E-recording is open to title companies, law firms, banks and other businesses that regularly record land records.

The county says documents return in hours instead of days, and rejected documents can be fixed and resubmitted within hours. It lists four vendors:

  • Simplifile, which handles both transfer and non-transfer documents (1-800-460-5657)
  • Corporation Service Company, for non-transfer documents (1-866-652-0111)
  • Indecomm Global Services, for non-transfer documents (877-272-5250)
  • GOePN (888-325-3365, ext. 1)

A seller does not sign up for any of these. The title company or closing attorney does it.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Lake County Recorder will record it?
sections.html:
The instrument has to carry the name of the person who prepared it, in a legible printed, typed, stamped or signed form, such as "This instrument was prepared by" followed by a name. It also must state that the preparer took reasonable care to redact Social Security numbers, under penalty of perjury.

Before the deed goes to the County Auditor, the parties also complete a sales disclosure form. All parties to the conveyance sign it, and it goes first to the county assessor for review. The Auditor processes it after that and sends it on to the assessor, who keeps it for five years. Each parcel generally needs its own form.

The rule covers deeds and contracts of sale for value, and transfers by foreclosure, divorce, court order or probate. It excludes security instruments such as mortgages, short-term leases, utility easements and most quitclaim deeds. Questions about the Lake County Auditor's real estate desk go to 219-755-3157.

sections.h2: Is there a transfer tax when recording a deed in Lake County?
sections.html:
The documents we reviewed list recording fees, not a transfer tax. The recorder fee statute and the county Recorder page name recording and copy charges, and the county's Auditor real estate page was still a placeholder when we read it.

For a closing figure, call the Auditor at 219-755-3157 or the Recorder at 219-755-3730, or ask the title company for its settlement statement.

sections.h2: What is the story behind the Crown Point courthouse and the county seat?
sections.html:
Lake County was established in 1837 and Liverpool was its first seat. Lake Court House, later renamed Crown Point, was chosen as the seat in 1840. Solon Robinson and his family were the first settlers in the Crown Point area, arriving on October 31, 1834.

The Old Lake County Courthouse, nicknamed the Grand Old Lady, was begun in 1878 and expanded through 1928. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974, and a new Government Center opened the next year. Crown Point had 33,899 residents in 2020.

The Recorder's page lists one office, at 2293 N. Main Street. Lake County covers 626.5 square miles and has 19 incorporated cities and towns, so that office serves places as different as Gary, Hammond and Crown Point.

sections.h2: How do delinquent taxes show up when recording a Lake County sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax is a claim against the parcel, so a title search will turn it up before a deed is recorded. Lake County's 2026 tax sale began online on September 4, 2026, and redemption for certificates sold expires September 8, 2027.

A cash buyer works around these items the same way a title company does. Back taxes, liens and open mortgages are paid from the proceeds, releases are recorded, and the deed follows. The released liens are separate recordings with their own fees.

  • Gather the deed, the tax bill and any lien or mortgage payoff letters
  • Confirm the legal description and the parcel number
  • Sign the sales disclosure form and the deed at the title company
  • Let the title company record the deed and releases through a vendor or at the Recorder

sections.h2: Why do older Lake County properties need extra title attention?
sections.html:
Industry built much of the county. U.S. Steel founded Gary Works in 1906, and the county's population peaked at 546,253 in 1970 before falling to 498,700 in 2020. Gary's 2020 census counted 23.2% of its housing units as vacant.

Houses that have changed hands through estates, tax sales or long vacancies can carry old liens or unrecorded releases. Ask the title company to run the chain of title early so any missing release can be recorded before the closing date.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Lake County, Indiana?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded with the Lake County Recorder at 2293 N. Main Street, Building A, 2nd Floor in Crown Point. Title companies usually send them electronically.

faqs.q: How much does the Lake County Recorder charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Indiana Code lists $25 to record a deed or other instrument, and $55 for a mortgage. The county may add charges by ordinance, so ask the office for the current total.

faqs.q: Can I e-record in Lake County?
faqs.a: Yes, through approved vendors, but the service is open to businesses that regularly record land records, such as title companies and banks. Individuals normally use their closing agent.

faqs.q: What is a sales disclosure form in Indiana?
faqs.a: It is a form that every party to a covered conveyance signs before the deed is filed with the county auditor. The assessor reviews it first.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the Lake County Recorder?
faqs.a: Call 219-755-3730 on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. The fax number is (219) 648-6028.
